title: Chantries of many Traditions
summary: Why mages of different paths share a home.

claims.text: Over the last three centuries, Chantries that mix several Traditions have become the main power among Tradition mages.
Even in the Mythic Age some mages of differing paths or Hermetic houses pooled their efforts, and Technocratic expansion made such teamwork the rule.
Many see mixed cabals as a needed adaptation; more conservative factions still prefer a Chantry of one Tradition.

title: The great Chantries
summary: The oldest and largest Tradition strongholds.

claims.text: The great Chantries have built Realms rarely under 200 miles across, with their own ecosystems and inhabitants, shaped by the will of their founders.
Their buildings are vast, staffed by more Acolytes than needed, and usually keep an earthly site plus one or more outposts.
Their covenants run long and dry on fine parchment, and apprentices copy them by hand; each new situation adds another clause.

title: Doissetep in its prime
summary: The greatest Tradition Chantry as it stood in the early 1990s.

claims.text: Doissetep, the Chantry of Cal Ladeim, sits in the Shard Realm of Forces behind black walls and towers heavy with gargoyles.
It is the largest Chantry known, home to ten cabals, each chasing its own agenda and each wanting to rule.
Outside attack can hardly touch it, but it is rotting from within, and Ascension is half forgotten amid the struggle for control.
The Panel of Deacons, the oldest common form, seats either the leading cabal or one voice from each cabal, each with an equal vote; Technocratic Constructs call such bodies Amalgam Primes.
Older Chantries often answer to one leader, who may be elected, may have to prove fitness, or in Progenitor Constructs may have to fight for the seat.
Politics among council members runs on alliances, favors owed and trickery, and outright dictators are not unknown.

title: Opening a new Node
summary: How mages create a fresh source of Quintessence.

claims.text: Finding a site means a trip into the Near Umbra to locate a spot where the Tapestry is loose enough to channel Quintessence.
Each faction has its own way: Dreamspeakers petition spirits, Akashic Brothers meditate for days, Virtual Adepts work out the proof in mathematics.
All agree the job is perilous and best done by a whole cabal, since a mistake can draw Paradox or set off a chain reaction.

title: The New World Order's rise
summary: How the information Convention gained its edge.

claims.text: While other Conventions focused on building science, the New World Order gathered information, storing it in early living computers made with help from the Sons of Ether.
Its power grew through the 1800s as it infiltrated groups, among them the first mixed Tradition Chantries, and it became the Technocracy's internal police.
